checks: The strict signs make all diagonal/off-diagonal magnitudes positive. Summing the balanced normal evaluations at each vertex gives exactly the asserted column identity.

The cap is the simplex cut off at the unique included vertex. Along each edge from that vertex the zero margin occurs at a_i/(a_i+b_ij). Taking the determinant of the scaled edge columns gives the product formula for the actual cap volume fraction.

The cap pyramid height is H a_i/||v_i||, so the physical section measure divided by ||v_i|| is d|K|q_i/(Ha_i). Consequently the inverse coarea has common multiplier H/(d²|K|) times f_i/q_i^((d−1)/d). This keeps the scale of the balanced normals.

After the substitution x_j=a_i+b_ij, f_i is d times the geometric mean and g_i their sum. The column sums give total d+1. AM–GM on the square roots gives the variance bound; the pairwise square identity yields exactly the factor 1/d.
In d=1 the section is one point and its 0-dimensional measure is one. The only off-diagonal channel equals a_i+a_j=1, so both f_i equal one, the row deficit is zero, and the pair sum is empty.
The original source digest matches. §§1–2 contain the geometric normalization and variance argument, and §6 supplies the d=1 case.

overlap.comparison: Uses the same determinant product for edge intercepts but optimizes the cap of an individual vertex with a given mark. It does not give the coarea scale or a multirow balanced-normal variance budget.
Gives coarea continuity and an explicit barycentric cut at the simplex centroid. It does not derive the exact coarea for all strictly isolated vertex cuts with a common normal-balance scale.

readability: Here the volume fractions and section coareas refer only to the actual given simplex, with no mixing of sections from other fibers.

summary: The cap fractions and coareas are exact for the given simplex, and the row variance deficit has the stated constant in every dimension.
